# Scales: what did not land on a package step

Design card: **[design#1555](https://github.com/DevExpress/design/issues/1555)** — the review happens there; it does not block the release of the theme.

Material for the design team. Every category is marked in the code, so this inventory is reproducible and cannot drift from the sources. No unmarked fixed size is left in the theme: `tests/fluent-next-size-markers.test.ts` fails on the first px literal without a marker, so a new place either gets a category or does not pass.

The "step" column is computed: the value is converted to rem at a 16px root and looked up in the package scale. A filled cell means "a step with exactly this value already exists", an empty one means "no such step in the scale".

| Category | Marker | Places | Question |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Sizes off the scales | `dx-offscale` | 66 | which values deserve a step |
| A2. Sizes taken from another family's scale | `dx-foreign-scale` | 6 | does the property's own scale deserve these steps |
| B. Step exists, role does not | `dx-no-semantic-role` | 16 | which steps deserve semantic roles |
| B2. Icon glyph sizes | `dx-icon-glyph-size` | 23 | does the package need an icon size scale |
| C. Proportional values | `dx-relative` | 37 | do proportional values need DS roles |
| D. Computed sizes | `calc()` | 310 | what to compute at build time and what at runtime |
| E. Pixel nudges | `dx-px-nudge` | 70 | should the correction follow the scale or stay absolute |
| F. Shadow geometry | `dx-shadow-geometry` | 35 | a shadow role as a whole, rather than steps for its numbers |
| G. Border and line thickness | `dx-line-width` | 32 | put them on border-width steps, or must a hairline stay 1px |
| H. Must stay a number | `dx-literal-required` | 9 | no decision needed — the value is frozen by the technique |
| I. Fixed sizes written into rules | `dx-fixed-size` | 76 | does it deserve a step, or does the size stay fixed |
| K. Not a designed size | `dx-structural` | 19 | no decision needed — the number is a technique, not a size |

## A. Sizes off the scales — `dx-offscale`, 66

A named theme size with no matching step in any relevant package scale: the value stayed a px literal.

Distinct values: **38**. Most frequent: `-1px` ×8, `400px` ×4, `300px` ×4, `250px` ×3, `180px` ×3, `1.5px` ×3, `200px` ×2, `182px` ×2, `280px` ×2, `600px` ×2, `240px` ×2, `340px` ×2.

A step with the same value exists for **8** of 66 (the scale family is chosen by the property, `spacing` by default).

## A2. Sizes taken from another family's scale — `dx-foreign-scale`, 6

A length read from the spacing scale although the property has a scale of its own - a font size, a border width - because that scale has no step at the value. Unlike A the number is not a literal: it does sit on a scale, just not the one the property belongs to, so nothing looks wrong until you read which family the step came from. Unlike B a role could not be attached even if the package wanted one, because there is no step to attach it to. A value that DOES exist in the right family is not listed here - that is a plain mistake and gets fixed, not classified.

Distinct values: **5**. Most frequent: `spacing-130` ×2, `spacing-170` ×1, `spacing-80` ×1, `spacing-70` ×1, `spacing-340` ×1.

A step with the same value exists for **0** of 6 (the scale family is chosen by the property, `font-size` by default).

## C. Proportional values — `dx-relative`, 37

The value is proportional to the font size or to the container. It cannot become an absolute token without changing behaviour: em is measured from the element's font size, a token from the root.

Distinct values: **27**. Most frequent: `0.85em` ×4, `4em` ×3, `2em` ×3, `.125em` ×2, `0.2em` ×2, `1.428571` ×2, `1.3333` ×2, `3em` ×2, `17.14em` ×1, `4.85em` ×1, `12em` ×1, `2.2em` ×1.

## D. Computed sizes — calc(), 310 expressions per bundle

A token arrives in CSS as `var()`, so Sass can no longer fold the arithmetic: everything that used to be computed at build time is now computed by the browser. For comparison, the built legacy fluent has **50** `calc()` expressions and not one of them with a token.

| Class | Expressions | Why |
|---|---|---|
| identically zero | 0 | the same variable is subtracted from itself: `(X − X − 0) / 2`. In the legacy themes those calls took the numeric branch of the mixin and Sass folded the expression into `0`. |
| token and px literal | 15 | the derived value is computed from a token, but the correction stayed absolute — the value no longer scales along with the step. |
| multiplied by a factor | 28 | a magic multiplier with no matching step — a candidate either for a new step or for a token of its own. |
| arithmetic over tokens | 267 | an honest derived value: a difference or a fraction of steps. This is what var() is for — when the scale changes the value follows on its own. |

## E. Pixel nudges — `dx-px-nudge`, 70

An absolute addition or subtraction on top of a token. When the scale moves the derived value follows and the correction does not — on a large step ±1px goes unnoticed, on a small one it is a visible fraction of the size.

Distinct values: **14**. Most frequent: `1px` ×34, `2px` ×13, `-1px` ×11, `6px` ×4, `-2px` ×2, `3px` ×1, `4px` ×1, `0.5px` ×1, `-7px` ×1, `-6px` ×1, `9px` ×1, `8px` ×1.

A step with the same value exists for **60** of 70 (the scale family is chosen by the property, `spacing` by default).

## K. Not a designed size — `dx-structural`, 19

An off-screen parking coordinate (top: -9999px), a one-pixel probe, a number chosen to be far outside the viewport rather than to be seen. Nobody designs it and no step can replace it: making it a token would only invite someone to tune it. Unlike H, the value is not frozen by a syntax — it is frozen by having no visual meaning.

Distinct values: **7**. Most frequent: `1px` ×6, `-5000px` ×4, `-9999px` ×3, `0.1px` ×2, `-10px` ×2, `-100000px` ×1, `10px` ×1.
